patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 4's actuator structure, rotor galleries/ports, chamber communications, angular port-block function, operating routes, external pump/reservoir, and mechanical load context are supported by the cited patent passages. No unsupported numeric performance values or invented valve architecture are asserted.

functional_completeness.rationale: The formerly missing rotor-arm/chamber route and stator pressure/return context routes are now represented. Core pressurization, displaced-fluid return, rotor output, and conditional position-limit bypass are captured. Optional disclosed variants are explicitly omitted from this draft.

flow_consistency.rationale: Hydraulic and rotary flows use compatible port types; flow directions are compatible (including inout drain/reservoir paths). The action descriptions agree with the modeled paths and cited operating cases.

claim_traceability.rationale: Claimed apparatus elements and claim 11/12 operating behaviors are traceable to the cited passages. No fabricated requirements or constraints are introduced.

interfaces.rationale: Supply, drain/return, bore-to-rotor-base, rotor-to-chamber, stator-hole-to-chamber, stator pressure/return context, and rotary load interfaces have compatible existing endpoints. Shared pump/reservoir ports reflect selectable operating connections rather than simultaneous fixed routing.

textbook_application.rationale: External pump, reservoir, and driven load are modeled as distinct context components, consistent with textbook boundary/context guidance. The textbook is not used as evidence for invention facts.

summary: Independently reviewed saved SJS revision 4. Read all cited patent passages and relevant textbook guidance. The prior connectivity gaps are resolved: rotor arm ports now connect to the chamber, and stator routing has pump/reservoir context connections. Modeled behavior and interfaces align with patent operating descriptions; no unresolved issues identified. No candidate edits made.
